domain: Memory after HBM, 2026-2300 (HBM4/4E/5+ and custom base dies, 3D DRAM, oxide-semiconductor DRAM, FeRAM/FeFET, MRAM, RRAM, PCM, 3D NAND/HBF, compute-in-memory, monolithic 3D on logic, far-future storage) for a Mercury-built Dyson-swarm AI system
summary: Memory after HBM, 2026-2300. HBM is gone before the swarm launches (2045-2060): pods move to memory bonded on logic (custom HBM4E bases ~2027, zHBM/3D DRAM 2030-2040; KAIST HBM8 2038 is the last HBM-like part, 200-240 GB and 180 W per stack). The film needs no DRAM at all: radiation sets the split. A film chiplet absorbs 142-466 krad(Si) in 10 yr at 0.92 AU (ESP/SAPPHIRE 50-95 %, calibrated to NASA 4 mm Al doses), and local shields saturate near 20-100 krad, so DRAM/HBM (2-100 krad), 3D NAND (10-50 krad) and probably IGZO 2T0C stay in 5 g/cm2 pods (0.4-3.3 krad), while MRAM (>=1 Mrad), RRAM (5-20 Mrad), HZO FeRAM (10 Mrad) and SRAM live on the film. Stacked radiation-tolerant NVM lifts a 0.15 W chiplet from 16 MB (107 MB/W) to 0.13-4 GB in 2040 (mid 1 GB, 6.8 GB/W), 1-32 GB in 2070 and 4-256 GB in 2100+, against pods at 0.4 / 4 / 10 GB/W; the useful minimum (GPU bytes per FLOP/s) is 0.23 / 0.9 / 1.7 GB. SRAM shrinks to 1-2 MB, so leakage falls from 10-59 % to 1-10 % of chip power at 85 C; Tj stays 85-105 C because logic, not memory, sets it. The state for a 1e28-FLOP MoE replica stays ~1.1-1.4 PB (bytes/param 20 -> 5, sparsity 20 -> 100), so film power per replica falls 13.5 -> 0.21 -> 0.025 -> 0.008 MW; frontier patches shrink from 17-30 m to 3-12 m (compute-limited near 3-9 m); the replica-sized sail falls from 279 m to 62 m (1e29, 2040) and 22-38 m (1e30), so sail size reverts to structural optimum (150-300 m, many replicas). Memory-driven pod share drops 15 % -> 5 % (2040) -> 1 % (2070) -> ~0.3 % (2100+), cutting swarm mass per W by 30-47 %. New limits: local read energy must fall to 4-36 fJ/bit by 2070 (compute-in-memory or batch >=100), and Mercury lacks In, Pt, Ru, W, Te, so swarm-scale memory must be SiOx/TiOx RRAM, Zr- or MgZnO-ferroelectrics, Fe/MgO MTJs, In-free oxides and glass archives.

model_parameters.notes: Ranges 8-24 / 128-4096 / 1024-32768 / 4096-262144. 2026 = 4-8 MB SRAM + eMRAM/eRRAM; 2040 = BEOL cross-point MRAM/FeRAM/RRAM decks or a bonded 3D ferroelectric die; later vertical 3D NVM. Useful minimum = 2026-GPU bytes per FLOP/s: 30/225/900/1650 MB.
x0.8 usable fill for replicas/patches. Was the 107 MB/W basis.

model_parameters.unit: MB per W of pod chip power
model_parameters.notes: 2026 Rubin HBM4; 2040 HBM8-class/zHBM (KAIST ~6 TB per 15.4 kW); then 3D DRAM/FeRAM on logic. Film MB/W overtakes pods by ~2035-2040 because the film can stack NVM on every chiplet with no concentration penalty.
Only buffers/registers once weights, KV and optimizer state move to NVM/oxide memory.
1 MB: 0.8-4.9 % at 85 C, 1.4-16 % at 105 C, 2.5-50 % at 125 C (cells.py). The leakage cap on Tj goes away up to ~105 C.

Memory no longer sets the limit; logic does. FLOP/s/kg vs 85 C: 105 C 0.93x (2026 slope) / 1.00x (2100 slope); 125 C 0.85x / 0.97x (swarm.json). Hotter only pays for staying inside Earth orbit at high coverage.
5 g/cm2 gives 0.4-3.3 krad per 10 yr: still at the HBM/DRAM 2 krad onset in the 95 % environment; NAND fine. Pods that keep only archives and rad-tolerant NVM can drop to ~1 g/cm2 (3.7-27 krad).
BF16+FP32 Adam -> FP8 + 8-bit states -> FP4/FP8 + 4-bit states.
Nearly constant: bytes/param fall 4x while sparsity rises 5x, so total params for 1e28 FLOP grow 58T -> 115T -> 185T -> 289T.

Design-consistent scaling for the largest film replica (1e28, 1e29, 1e30, 1e30 FLOP). Below ~150 m the replica rule stops sizing sails: keep ~150-300 m for hub/vane fixed mass (2.4 % at 279 m, 19 % at 82 m) and pack 10-1000 replicas per sail.
Becomes compute-limited (2.8-9 m) for models whose weights fit in a few hundred thousand chiplets.
At batch 16 the budget is 62/16/4/4 fJ/bit: weight reads must become analog compute-in-memory or high-reuse batches by 2070.
HBM3E 3.44, HBM2 3.9; custom HBM4E ~1.7; DRAM on logic without PHY.
NVM weights survive brownouts and shadows; only KV/activations are volatile.

replaces_hbm.answer: HBM is replaced in two steps. (1) 2027-2035, in pods: custom logic base dies (HBM4E on N3P, ~2x efficiency), then memory bonded directly on the accelerator (Samsung zHBM, no interposer) with HBF/3D-NAND tiers for read-mostly weights; KAIST-roadmap HBM8 (2038, 200-240 GB, 64 TB/s, 180 W per stack) is the last HBM-like form. (2) 2035-2045, on the film: radiation-tolerant NVM (cross-point MRAM/FeRAM/RRAM decks in the logic BEOL or a bonded 3D ferroelectric die) on every 0.15 W chiplet, 0.13-4 GB per chiplet (mid 1 GB, 6.8 GB/W vs HBM 0.115 GB/W). Volatile DRAM (incl. 3D DRAM) survives only in shielded pods: it tolerates 2-100 krad, while a film chiplet receives 140-470 krad per 10 yr.
replaces_hbm.pod_memory_2040: 3D DRAM stacked on logic (zHBM-class, 0.3-1 pJ/bit) + 3D FeRAM/NVDRAM; HBF/1000-layer NAND for weights and datasets (100-300 Gb/mm2); 0.2-2 GB/W; 5 g/cm2 shield
replaces_hbm.pod_memory_2070: monolithic 3D DRAM/FeRAM on logic for the residual DRAM-only CPU work; storage vaults of dense 3D charge-trap NVM and fused-silica optical archives (1.6 Gbit/mm3, Mercury SiO2); 1-20 GB/W
replaces_hbm.pod_memory_2100plus: no memory-driven pods; archives (glass) and switch/gateway pods only; any DRAM is a niche
replaces_hbm.first_launch_note: First launch is 2045-2060, so no HBM ever flies: the first pods already use memory-on-logic, and the first film chiplets should carry NVM, not SRAM-only weights.

architecture_implications.question: 1. What replaces HBM, and when? What is the memory of a pod in 2040, 2070, 2100+?
architecture_implications.answer: HBM is replaced in two steps. (1) 2027-2035, in pods: custom logic base dies (HBM4E on N3P, ~2x efficiency), then memory bonded directly on the accelerator (Samsung zHBM, no interposer) with HBF/3D-NAND tiers for read-mostly weights; KAIST-roadmap HBM8 (2038, 200-240 GB, 64 TB/s, 180 W per stack) is the last HBM-like form. (2) 2035-2045, on the film: radiation-tolerant NVM (cross-point MRAM/FeRAM/RRAM decks in the logic BEOL or a bonded 3D ferroelectric die) on every 0.15 W chiplet, 0.13-4 GB per chiplet (mid 1 GB, 6.8 GB/W vs HBM 0.115 GB/W). Volatile DRAM (incl. 3D DRAM) survives only in shielded pods: it tolerates 2-100 krad, while a film chiplet receives 140-470 krad per 10 yr.

architecture_implications.question: 2. Capacity per 0.15 W chiplet once weights and KV sit in stacked NVM / near-zero-leakage memory; does the SRAM-leakage problem go away?
architecture_implications.answer: 2040: 128 MB-4 GB (mid 1 GB = 6.8 GB/W); 2070: 1-32 GB (mid 8 GB = 55 GB/W); 2100+: 4-256 GB (mid 32 GB = 218 GB/W). The useful minimum (2026-GPU bytes per FLOP/s) is 0.23 / 0.9 / 1.7 GB. Yes: with 1-2 MB of SRAM left, leakage is 0.8-10 % of chip power at 85 C and 1.4-31 % at 105 C (vs 10-59 % for 16 MB), NVM standby is zero and oxide 2T0C refresh is <=15 uW/GB even at 125 C. But the film optimum stays 85-105 C because logic J/op rises with T (FLOP/s/kg at 105 C = 0.93-1.00x of 85 C), so the gain is chip power returned to compute (+10-50 %), not a hotter film.

architecture_implications.question: 4. Does the film need pods for memory reasons (CPU/DRAM work, storage, training state)?
architecture_implications.answer: Training state: no from ~2040 (film holds ~17x more per W than pods at mid values; 0.4-140x across the ranges). CPU/DRAM sandboxes: move onto 1-5 chiplets once MRAM/FeRAM main memory (>=1e10-1e15 writes, SEU-immune) is on the film (2045-2070). Storage: a 279 m sail at 8 GB/chiplet holds ~850 PB, and storage power is tiny, so only archives remain (glass, Mercury SiO2). Minimum pod share from memory: 10-20 % (2026) -> 2-10 % (2040) -> 0.3-3 % (2070) -> 0-1 % (2100+).

architecture_implications.question: 5. Radiation: which memories can live unshielded on the film at 0.92 AU?
architecture_implications.answer: Film chiplet 10-yr TID: 142-466 krad(Si) (SAPPHIRE 50 % to ESP 95 %, r^-2). Local Si pads cut it to 61-238 krad (0.1 mm, +2.7 % mass) or 34-154 krad (0.25 mm, +10 %) and saturate near 20-100 krad. On the film: SRAM (TID fine; SEU 2e4-5e6 upsets per 16 MB per 10 yr, ECC+scrub), STT/SOT-MRAM (>=1 Mrad), HfOx/SiOx RRAM (5-20 Mrad), HZO FeRAM/FeFET (10 Mrad: Pr -5 %), PCM. Pods only: DRAM/HBM (2-15 krad irregularities; space DDR4 100 krad), 3D NAND (BER rises at 10 krad), and oxide-semiconductor 2T0C (Vth shift at 50 krad: open question). A 5 g/cm2 pod gives 0.4-3.3 krad per 10 yr.

architecture_implications.question: Bandwidth energy: does capacity help if the weights must be read?
architecture_implications.answer: Only with reuse or compute-in-memory. With memory reads capped at 20 % of chip energy, the allowed local read energy at batch reuse 128 falls from 500 fJ/bit (2026) to 130 (2040) and 33-36 fJ/bit (2070-2100+); at reuse 16 it is 4 fJ/bit by 2070. Stacked NVM reads cost ~50-500 fJ/bit today, so by ~2060 weight memory must be analog/digital compute-in-memory arrays (Study 1 analog CIM) or serve batches of >=100-1000.

architecture_implications.question: Manufacturability from Mercury materials
architecture_implications.answer: At GB/chiplet the active layers need 0.5-300 g of scarce element per MW. Mercury rock shell (8e22 kg) caps: In (IGZO) at f ~0.003-0.03 (1 GB/chiplet) and 0.00005-0.0005 (32 GB); Sn (ZTO) at f ~0.03-0.3 (1 GB); Hf (HZO, HfO2 RRAM) at f ~0.2-0.4 (1 GB) and ~0.003-0.007 (32 GB); Pt/Ru/W MTJ layers and Te (GST) at f ~1e-6-1e-2; W word-line NAND at f <1e-3. Zr (10.8 ppm) and Co carry to f ~0.1-1. So swarm-scale memory must be built from Si, O, Mg, Al, Ti, Fe, Zr (+ trace Zn, Sn): SiOx/TiOx/AlOx RRAM, ZrO2-rich or Mg-ZnO ferroelectrics, Fe/MgO MTJs without Pt/Ru/W/B, In-free oxide channels, poly-Si/TiSi word lines, fused-silica archives.
